name: anthropic-cookbook
description: Claude API examples and practical recipes for tool use, retrieval, structured outputs, and agent workflows.
pros: Official examples make API patterns easy to adapt
Broad coverage across common Claude application flows
Good reference for teams standardizing prompt and tool practices
cons: Examples still require production hardening
Repository breadth can make the first path hard to choose

name: awesome-claude
description: A curated directory of Claude projects, prompts, workflows, and community resources.
pros: Fast discovery across many Claude use cases
Useful map of community tools and integrations
Simple structure works well for evaluation lists
cons: Curated links vary in freshness
Quality and maintenance differ by linked project

name: claude-code
description: Command-line coding assistant patterns and resources for agentic development workflows.
pros: Targets real developer workflows instead of isolated demos
Strong fit for repository-local task execution
Helpful reference for code review and implementation loops
cons: Requires careful permissions and workspace hygiene
Best practices continue to evolve quickly

name: claude-engineer
description: An experimental coding agent that demonstrates file editing, command execution, and iterative development loops.
pros: Concrete example of agentic software engineering
Easy to inspect and modify for local experiments
Shows practical orchestration around Claude
cons: Experimental architecture may not fit production teams
Needs strict guardrails before sensitive use

name: claude-task-master
description: Task planning and project management workflow helpers designed for AI-assisted coding projects.
pros: Turns fuzzy work into trackable implementation tasks
Pairs well with coding assistants and PR workflows
Good for teams that want lightweight planning artifacts
cons: Planning output still needs human prioritization
Can add process overhead for small changes

name: claude-agents
description: Reusable agent definitions and patterns for multi-step Claude workflows.
pros: Good starting point for role-specific agents
Encourages repeatable instructions and responsibilities
Useful for comparing agent decomposition strategies
cons: Agent behavior depends heavily on surrounding tools
Templates need adaptation to local policies

name: claude-prompts
description: Prompt collections and reusable instruction patterns for Claude and other language models.
pros: Large prompt surface helps with quick ideation
Examples are easy to copy into experiments
Useful for comparing prompt framing styles
cons: Prompt quality is uneven across entries
Needs testing against current Claude models

name: mcp-servers
description: Reference Model Context Protocol servers that connect Claude-compatible clients to tools and data sources.
pros: Standardizes tool and data access patterns
Reference implementations speed up integration
Strong fit for workspace and enterprise workflows
cons: Operational security review is required for each server
Compatibility depends on client and server versions

name: claude-squad
description: A terminal workflow for managing multiple Claude coding sessions across tasks and repositories.
pros: Makes parallel coding sessions easier to track
Fits advanced users who already live in the terminal
Useful for coordinating independent implementation threads
cons: Terminal-first workflow has a learning curve
Parallel agents increase review and merge burden

name: claude-code-router
description: Routing utilities for Claude Code setups that need configurable model and provider selection.
pros: Helpful for advanced local Claude Code configurations
Separates routing concerns from day-to-day coding work
Can simplify experiments across provider settings
cons: Adds another moving part to debug
Requires careful configuration management
